models.collectorNote: Fibreglass doesn't rust but it does craze and the chassis beneath it does rust; the R is the valuable one and its disc-brake hardware should all be present.

generations.name: 541 / 541R / 541S
generations.note: The standard car's Austin DS5 engine made about 130 hp as fitted; the R's higher-compression tune is commonly quoted at 150 hp. Just over 500 541s of all kinds were built.

models.intro: Jensen's fibreglass pioneer: a glass-bodied GT with Austin's four-litre six, a Perspex rear window and a drag figure that embarrassed steel cars. The 541R added disc brakes all round, a British first on a production four-seater, and the 541S finished the line in comfort.

models.collectorNote: About 500 were built and survival is low; originality of the fibreglass nose, often repaired, sometimes re-shaped, is the inspection's first item.

generations.name: C-V8 Mk I–III
generations.note: The 361 cu in engine of the first cars gave way to the 383. The FF experiment, Ferguson four-wheel drive and anti-lock brakes, was proven on a C-V8 before it reached the Interceptor.

models.intro: Before the Interceptor, the formula: Chrysler V8 power in a West Bromwich fibreglass body, with the canted quad headlamps that half the press hated and the other half never forgot. One of the fastest four-seaters of its day, full stop.
models.name: C-V8

models.collectorNote: FFs and SPs sit at the top; rust in the sills and rear arches decides everything else. Chrysler mechanicals are the easy part, trim and that rear glass are not.

generations.name: Interceptor Mk I / Mk II (+ FF)
generations.note: The FF (1966–71) added Ferguson Formula four-wheel drive and Dunlop Maxaret anti-lock brakes, the first production car with either, let alone both. About 320 FFs were built.

generations.name: Interceptor Mk III / SP
generations.note: The 440 cu in engine arrived with the Mk III; the six-pack SP's triple carburettors made it the most powerful Jensen at a quoted 390 hp, and one of the fastest four-seaters in the world in 1971.

models.intro: The definitive Jensen: Touring of Milan's steel body, that vast curved rear window, Chrysler V8 torque, and in the FF, four-wheel drive and anti-lock brakes years before Audi made the quattro famous. It was the car rock stars bought instead of an Aston, and it has never stopped looking like money.
models.name: Interceptor

models.collectorNote: Timing-belt history is the engine's whole file, the 907 is an interference engine. The shooting-brake Jensen GT is the rarity.

generations.name: Jensen-Healey Mk I / Mk II
generations.note: The Lotus 907 was its first production home, before the Esprit. About 10,000 Jensen-Healeys were built; the five-speed Mk II cars are the developed ones.

models.intro: Jensen's bid for the American sports-car market after the Big Healey ended: Donald Healey's name, a Lotus twin-cam engine, and styling built for California. Engine teething troubles hurt it early; sorted cars are the quick, comfortable classic the spec sheet always promised.
models.name: Jensen-Healey
